name: Inductor

claims.claim_text: An inductor is the circuit element to which energy stored in a magnetic field is assigned; the lumped identification of a component as an inductor, capacitor or resistor is valid only while the physical object is small compared with the wavelength of the signals passing through it.
claims.quote_verbatim: if the energy is stored primarily electrostatically, you call that a capacitor. If it's stored in the magnetic field, you call that an inductor
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: Once structures approach the size of a wavelength, energy can no longer be localised as purely magnetic in one place and purely electrostatic in another, and the circuit must be treated as distributed rather than as separate inductors and capacitors.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can no longer talk about a capacitor and an inductor as being separate entities
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: The relation V = L di/dt serves as the working mental model for inductive behaviour: current flowing in an inductor that is then interrupted by a switch produces a voltage spike, which is the same mechanism behind boost-converter operation and relay-coil kickback.
claims.quote_verbatim: if there's current going through that inductor and a switch shuts off somewhere, I'm going to have a voltage spike
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Kirchhoff's current law is a special-case derivation of Maxwell's equations and does not hold in the presence of a changing magnetic field, which is what an inductor produces; measured currents around such a loop do not sum to zero.
claims.quote_verbatim: it doesn't hold in the presence of a magnetic field. Right? A change in magnetic field, which is what an inductor is
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: When the magnetic core of an inductor or transformer saturates the part stops behaving as an inductor and presents little more than the DC resistance of its winding, so the current is limited only by the copper.
claims.quote_verbatim: when a magnetic core of a transformer or an inductor saturates, it ceases to become an inductor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Core saturation in a switching supply shows up as a primary-side meltdown with the secondary side intact and the input fuse blown, while the unit may still briefly power up and drive its display before failing.
claims.quote_verbatim: The secondary side works fine. And it was the primary side that just melted down.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An audibly singing inductor in a switching converter is a symptom of a control loop that is badly compensated rather than a defect in the inductor; a converter designed before high-value ceramic output capacitors were available can be destabilised by them and by its load.
claims.quote_verbatim: Last time I ran into a singing inductor, it was exactly that issue, actually. It was bad compensation, and then the inductor ended up singing because of it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Capacitors, Simulation and Closures - Deonerated Design Dealmaking

claims.claim_text: Powering a boost converter from a source-measure unit into an active load can cause its control loop to lose regulation, driving the output voltage too high and destroying the switching transistor; the same board worked normally from an ordinary bench supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: So now it's driving an inductor. It gets out of control. It's control loop and the voltage gets too high and it probably popped the fat on it

claims.claim_text: An assembly error in which inductors are populated in place of decoupling capacitors presents at power-up as an apparent short across the supply rail, because the parts share the same passive package and are indistinguishable by inspection.
claims.quote_verbatim: the 10 nanofarad decoupling capacitors were inductors
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin O'Flynn - Aspirated Adamantine Attacks

claims.claim_text: Within a single inductor series at a fixed physical size, current rating falls sharply as inductance rises: a 1 microhenry part rated at 1.8 amps sits in the same series as a 100 microhenry part rated at roughly 100 milliamps.
claims.quote_verbatim: the one micro henry inductor in the same series all in the same series was rated at 1.8 amps but the 100 micro henry one was rated for like 100 milliamps
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Inductance and current rating trade against each other at constant package size because more inductance requires more turns, which requires finer wire; getting both simultaneously requires a physically larger part.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need a smaller gauge wire you've got to wind more of them on there to get your increased henries and uh the current current rating drops
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A requirement of around 2.3 amps in a small surface-mount inductor is demanding enough that general-purpose inductor sample kits will not contain a suitable part.
claims.quote_verbatim: i couldn't find a suitable inductor i've got three huge inductor kits that you know i still couldn't find one to do the job
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A height-constrained inductor can have very low DC resistance, on the order of a milliohm or less, and still perform poorly because its core losses dominate; allowing a taller part lowers core loss and improves the overall result.
claims.quote_verbatim: it may have, you know, a milli-ohm or less a DCR, but the core losses are through the roof
claims.speaker: Carmen Parisi
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: Mechanical z-height limits set by the product, rather than electrical requirements, frequently decide which inductor a power converter can use, so the strictness of a stated height limit is worth interrogating early in a design.
claims.quote_verbatim: when a customer says we have this height requirement, you always got to ask how, how strict is that
claims.speaker: Carmen Parisi
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: Designing a switching converter from a controller data sheet is a long calculation sequence, on the order of thirty equations, in which the inductor peak current is computed first, an inductor is then selected against it, and that part's DC resistance is fed back into the loss calculation.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to calculate, you know, the inductor peak current, and then you've got to actually go find the inductor

claims.claim_text: For production runs of only a handful of units, an off-the-shelf power module is usually cheaper than a discrete switching design, because the engineering time spent selecting the MOSFET and inductor, working the calculations and chasing possible oscillation dominates the component cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want to have to dick around with, you know, selecting the right MOSFET and inductor and going through all the calculations and then hoping it doesn't bloody oscillate on you

claims.claim_text: Switch-mode power supplies of the early 2010s typically topped out around 500 kilohertz, with a physically substantial inductor carrying on the order of an amp.
claims.quote_verbatim: a beefy inductor switching, like, an amp of current
claims.episode_title: Moore's Law, GaN and SiC devices - Gallimaufry GaN Gabble

claims.claim_text: Raising switching frequency reduces inductor size but eventually runs into a wall where parasitic capacitance and parasitic inductance in the layout and components dominate; the efficiency curve peaks and then falls, defining a sweet spot for the operating frequency.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no point going up in frequency anymore because your losses
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moore's Law, GaN and SiC devices - Gallimaufry GaN Gabble

claims.claim_text: At sufficiently high switching frequencies the required inductance becomes small enough that a loop of PCB trace can serve as the converter inductor instead of a discrete wound part.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you only need tiny inductors or you can use parasitic inductors. You can do board-level inductors just doing a loop on a board kind of thing.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moore's Law, GaN and SiC devices - Gallimaufry GaN Gabble

claims.claim_text: Faster switching devices permit smaller inductors in a power converter, which matters because inductors are among the heaviest and most expensive parts in the converter and are also the main source of stray magnetic field.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I have a faster switching, I can have smaller inductors. And that's really important because inductors are heavy and expensive

claims.claim_text: Motor-control PWM typically runs in the 10 to 30 kilohertz range while digital power conversion runs at 100 kilohertz and above; the higher frequency is what allows the digital-power inductors to be physically smaller.
claims.quote_verbatim: anywhere from like 10 to 30, somewhere in there. Digital power, you're looking at 100 kilohertz plus
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: A device requiring several separately regulated high-current rails needs a switching regulator and inductor per rail, and the resulting inductors can occupy more board area than the FPGA or system-on-chip they supply, adding cost and cutting efficiency.
claims.quote_verbatim: Just the inductors alone can be bigger than the entire FPGA
claims.episode_title: Tesla, FPGAs and DigiKey - Zesty Zippy Zynq

claims.claim_text: A push-pull controller alternately switches a high-side and a low-side transistor to drive a transformer or inductor, transferring power that is then stepped up or down and rectified on the far side.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can transfer power through a transformer or an inductor and then you can step it up, step it down, and then you can rectify it on the other side

claims.claim_text: A boost converter works by driving current through an inductor and abruptly interrupting it, so that the resulting voltage spike is rectified through a diode into an output capacitor; a complete implementation can consist of an inductor, a diode, two capacitors and a four-pin switching IC.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's a inductor, diode, two caps and the actual switcher itself, a four pin switcher.

claims.claim_text: Processor core rails are supplied by the ordinary buck topology, taking anything from about 5 volts to 22 volts down to roughly a volt, but at any appreciable power the single buck is replicated into a multi-phase buck of parallel switch-and-inductor sets sharing common input and output capacitors.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get your upper and lower fat, you drive an inductor, then there's an output capacitor, uh, a multi-phase buck. You have another set
claims.speaker: Carmen Parisi
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: Paralleling N buck phases gives an effective inductance of L divided by N, so the converter can slew output current far faster and needs less output capacitance than a single phase attempting to supply 150 to 200 amps; the input and output ripple cancellation this yields depends on the quality of the layout.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have multiple bucks in parallel, you get L divided by the number of phases. So you can slew more current quicker. So you can use less output capacitance
claims.speaker: Carmen Parisi
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: A transformer is an inductor with a second inductor coupled to it, so a standard buck converter can be used to drive a transformer winding rather than a plain inductor.
claims.quote_verbatim: a transformer is just an inductor with another inductor coupled to it
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Coupling a second winding onto a buck converter's inductor turns it into a transformer and gives the converter flyback-like behaviour in addition to its buck action.
claims.quote_verbatim: instead of using just an inductor, they're coupling that and using it as a transformer as well
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: A 200 volt Nixie supply can be built as a flyback by treating one winding of a small 10:1 transformer as a plain inductor: the winding is clamped to ground to charge from a 5 volt rail and then released, and the ten-times voltage appearing on the secondary is dumped through a diode into a capacitor.
claims.quote_verbatim: you use one leg of the transformer and pretend it's an inductor. So you like clamp it to ground. The other side is hooked up to five volts, charges up, and then you let go of that one side and it flips up.
claims.speaker: CNLohr

claims.claim_text: A microcontroller GPIO with 50 milliamps of drive capability can switch the flyback MOSFET of a high-voltage supply directly, without a separate gate driver, with a second GPIO used for feedback.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's got 50 milliamps of drive current
claims.speaker: CNLohr

claims.claim_text: An LED can be driven from an inductor's flyback rather than from a resistor: a short PWM-triggered current pulse energises the inductor and the LED sits across it as the flyback element, with brightness set by the current and duration of the energising pulse.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you control the amount of current and time that you energize the inductor for
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: An LED has one specific drive current at which it converts electrical energy to light most efficiently, set by die size and device physics; efficiency falls above that current through droop and also falls at very low currents, so pulsing at the efficient current beats a large series resistor for a long-lived dim indicator.
claims.quote_verbatim: Above that, you get what's called droop, which is one of the big factors in LED lighting.
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: In a high-current isolated supply, the rectified transformer output is a square wave, so a large inductance follows the secondary diodes to smooth it.
claims.quote_verbatim: after the, the secondary diodes, you, you go to a big inductance
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: The Raspberry Pi RP2350 integrates a switching regulator that takes a 3.3 volt input and generates the core supplies, but still requires an external inductor and external capacitors.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have an external inductor and some external caps
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A vendor hardware design guide that has to specify the orientation in which a switching-regulator inductor is installed indicates a marginal choice of part; a larger inductor and different layout would remove the sensitivity rather than pushing the constraint onto assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: All they're doing is in their design guide is actually recommending that you install the inductor the right way around.

claims.claim_text: Surface-mount air-core inductors differ between manufacturers in the axis of their winding: some are wound with the coil cylinder lying flat on the board and others with it standing vertically. In a differential LC filter, two closely spaced horizontal-axis parts couple enough to act as a common-mode transformer and give good common-mode rejection, so substituting vertical-axis parts of identical value destroys the rejection.
claims.quote_verbatim: if the cylinders are horizontal, there is enough coupling
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: When a qualified LC filter fails on a customer board while simulation predicts correct behaviour, the diagnostic sequence is to sweep the filter, measure the inductors in circuit, then desolder them and measure value, Q factor, drift and tolerance; if all of those are within specification the fault lies in the physical arrangement rather than the components, a distinction that can take days to isolate.
claims.quote_verbatim: We measured the Q factor of the inductor. We desolded these parts. We measured them for drift and tolerance.
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: A class D amplifier needs a physically large output inductor, and the finite resistance of its winding dissipates enough heat at maximum volume to make thermal headroom a layout and packaging constraint alongside the space constraint.
claims.quote_verbatim: you typically need a pretty big output inductor on some of these. That's going to start to get warm at max volume because it's got some finite resistance.
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: A class D output stage uses two second-order LC filters, and the inductors and capacitors must be arranged so that the fluxes cancel and the impedances at each end are balanced; an imbalance produces an audible click or pop at start-up and shows up on radiated-emission scans.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to figure out the right configuration of inductors and the correct configuration of capacitors to make sure that, uh, your fluxes are canceling out
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: The efficiency for which class D amplifiers are known applies at high output levels; at normal low listening levels the loss in the output filter inductors dominates, and addressing that region was reported to cut power consumption there by a factor of ten.
claims.quote_verbatim: Then you have a big loss in your inductors, uh, with your filter there.
claims.speaker: Jørgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: Active filters built around amplifiers run out of usefulness above roughly five megahertz, so signal-conditioning filters at higher frequencies are built from real inductors instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: You'll use a filter that has like inductors and, um, you know, instead of using amplifiers to do the, the thing that inductors do, you just use inductors

claims.claim_text: Cleaning up a switching supply's output can be done either with a large output LC filter or with a tracking linear post-regulator; the tracking regulator costs efficiency but a low-dropout part need only sit a few hundred millivolts above the output.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to put, like, some huge L's and C's on the output. Or the only other way to do it is to have some sort of tracking regulator on the output

claims.claim_text: A switching supply's output noise must be characterised across its whole load range rather than at one operating point, because output capacitor effectiveness falls with rising current and interacts with the inductor and with a switching frequency that may itself vary with load.
claims.quote_verbatim: the higher your current, the less effective your output caps become and stuff like that. It's in combination with your inductors and in combination with the frequency, which might change with load as well.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Inductor values in shipping designs are routinely altered late and empirically to pass radiated-emissions testing; a documented case is a 20 microhenry change made for FCC compliance.
claims.quote_verbatim: Inductor change by 20 micro-Henrys because of FCC testing. Right. Figured out empirically.

claims.claim_text: EMI reduction rests on understanding why low inductance and small loop area matter, so an EMI reference document that lists techniques without their underlying reasoning is a lookup aid rather than a substitute for the physics.
claims.quote_verbatim: why inductors matter, why low inductance matters

claims.claim_text: Inductors and transformers are among the few components an engineer can practically fabricate by hand, which is why they remain accessible in through-hole construction.
claims.quote_verbatim: certainly inductors and transformers can actually wind yourself
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Inductors, transformers and antennas can all be formed directly from PCB copper; because the board is being etched anyway, such structures cost nothing but the board area they occupy.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've done all three of those on PCBs just with tracers and they come for free because you're already etching the board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An extremely low-profile inductor can be built by winding the coil through the layers of a twelve- to sixteen-layer board and fitting a ferrite core through a hole drilled in the centre of the winding.
claims.quote_verbatim: you actually drill the hole in the middle and you put the ferrite over that and that gives you an extremely low profile
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The deflection yoke coil salvaged from a CRT television can be reused directly as an inductor of about 3 millihenries.
claims.quote_verbatim: I repurposed it as a 3 mH inductor
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Tuned circuits resonating at around 100 megahertz require inductors too large to integrate on a chip; Tom Lee's thesis work built an FM radio entirely in CMOS with no inductors by using gyrators, which synthesise an inductance from a capacitor and add electrical tunability at the cost of poor quality.
claims.quote_verbatim: to make tuned circuits that resonate at a hundred megahertz requires some fairly good size inductors, which you can't integrate
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: Large inductors and capacitors are not amenable to silicon integration or wafer-level assembly, so even a highly integrated single-chip or chiplet solution must place them on the package substrate or on the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: There are certain things that, that are just simply not friendly for silicon integration, things like big inductors and capacitors
claims.speaker: Ming Zhang

claims.claim_text: Complete DC-DC converter modules are built as a small PCB with the inductor mounted on top and the controller die embedded inside the board, in an SO-8 sized footprint and costing under fifteen cents in quantity; higher-current variants up to about six amps use the same die with a larger inductor.
claims.quote_verbatim: the higher power ones, I think, are probably the same chip with a bigger inductor on it. There's ones up to like 6 amps.

claims.claim_text: Precision passive filter manufacture before the era of tight component tolerances depended on in-house winding of inductors on dedicated machines and on individually measuring each capacitor and marking its actual value on the body.
claims.quote_verbatim: the company used to build things where you needed pretty precise inductors and pretty precisely known capacitors
claims.speaker: Kendall Castor-Perry

claims.claim_text: An inductance-to-digital converter senses metal in proximity by monitoring a resonant coil inductor, which is the operating principle of a stud finder.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just an inductor, like a resonant coil inductor. And then it tells when metal's nearby it

claims.claim_text: Electromagnetic fault injection uses an inductor as the probe tip and dumps a large, fast current pulse into it, since by V = L di/dt a strong localised magnetic field requires a large rate of change of current.
claims.quote_verbatim: it has an inductor at the end of it. You dump a really powerful, um, pulse. So really what you need is a big current change to generate a strong magnetic field.
claims.speaker: Colin O'Flynn
claims.episode_title: Shouting at chips with Colin O'Flynn
